$comment: THE RATCHET. Every cell in the registered population is enumerated here, including the unknown
ones, because a sparse baseline lists what is known -- so anything unknown is absent, so absence
`cells` is empty because the registered repository population is empty. That does NOT make this a
satisfied ratchet: checkRatchet reports POPULATION_EMPTY and the run exits non-zero, because a
control that holds over nothing is a false green rather than a clean one.
EDITED BY A HUMAN, ALWAYS. There is no --write, no --update-baseline and no regenerate switch
anywhere in this enforcer, and test/ratchet.test.mjs asserts that against the source. The reason is
transplanted from PredictionStandards/scripts/integrity.mjs: the first response to a red build
Each cell records the EXCLUSION RULES for that repository x pack -- the glob and its reason, as
configuration. It does not record what those rules matched. Ratcheting match counts would go red
every time a vendored tree grew by two files, and ADR 0007 already recorded where that leads.
